title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§52, previous page): for the quartic X = A + Bx + Cx^2 + Dx^3 + Ex^4 (Y and K the same polynomial at y and k), the equation dx/sqrt(X) - dy/sqrt(Y) = 0 with initial condition x = k when y = 0 has the Lagrange-type integral
[2A + B(x+y) + 2Cxy + Dxy(x+y) + 2Ex^2y^2 + 2 sqrt(XY)]/(x-y)^2 = [2A + Bk + 2 sqrt(AK)]/k^2.
The printed denominator is (x-y)^2. Check with X = 1 - x^2, x = sin a, y = sin b: the left side equals 4cos^2((a+b)/2) / [4cos^2((a+b)/2) sin^2((a-b)/2)] = 1/sin^2((a-b)/2). This is constant exactly when a - b is constant, so the signs are right.

This page, §53 (Corollary I, end). For D = E = 0 the quadratic case also has the simpler integral of Theorem III:
sqrt(XY) - (B/2)(x+y) - Cxy = sqrt(AK) - (B/2)k,
i.e. 2 sqrt(XY) = 2 sqrt(AK) - B(k - x - y) + 2Cxy.
Substituting this into the Lagrange form removes the radical in x, y. The integral becomes
[2A + B(2x+2y-k) + 4Cxy + 2 sqrt(A(A+Bk+Ck^2))]/(x-y)^2 = [2A + Bk + 2 sqrt(A(A+Bk+Ck^2))]/k^2.
Clearing denominators gives a symmetric relation of degree <= 2 in each variable, Euler's 'canonical' form alpha + 2beta(x+y) + gamma(x^2+y^2) + 2delta xy = 0. This is the algebraic addition law for the integral dx/sqrt(quadratic).

§54 (Corollary II). Take A = B = 0, so X = x^2(C + Dx + Ex^2). The equation becomes dx/(x sqrt(C+Dx+Ex^2)) = dy/(y sqrt(C+Dy+Ey^2)), with integral
[xy(2C + D(x+y) + 2Exy) + 2xy sqrt((C+Dx+Ex^2)(C+Dy+Ey^2))]/(x-y)^2 = Delta.
Euler notes that Delta cannot be fixed through k, because y = 0 is a singular point (dy/y diverges there). He still calls the integral memorable.

§55 (Corollary III). Substitute x -> 1/x, y -> 1/y. Then dx/(x sqrt(C+Dx+Ex^2)) becomes -du/sqrt(Cu^2+Du+E), so the equation is dy/sqrt(Cy^2+Dy+E) - dx/sqrt(Cx^2+Dx+E) = 0. The integral transforms to
[2Cxy + D(x+y) + 2E + 2 sqrt((Cx^2+Dx+E)(Cy^2+Dy+E))]/(y-x)^2 = Delta.
In this form y = 0 is admissible, giving Delta = [Dk + 2E + 2 sqrt(E(Ck^2+Dk+E))]/k^2.
On the next page Euler relabels (E, D, C) -> (A, B, C) and recovers Corollary I exactly, as a consistency check. In effect he uses the invariance of the Lagrange integral under the inversion x -> 1/x (reversal of the coefficients of the quartic) to handle the degenerate case.

All algebra on the page checks out.
errors: Printed typo on this page: the right-hand side of the first displayed formula reads '2A + BK + ...' with a capital K; it should be 'Bk' (lower case), as the derivation requires.
Corollary II: Delta is genuinely not determined by the y=0 normalization. Euler states this correctly; it is a remark, not a gap.

ideas.what: Eliminating the radical between Lagrange's symmetric integral and the elementary integral for a quadratic radicand, to obtain a symmetric quadratic algebraic relation between x and y
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic addition law for arcsine-type (genus 0 / conic) integrals; symmetric biquadratic (Euler's canonical equation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Institutiones calculi integralis; earlier papers on elliptic integrals, 1750s-60s); Lagrange 1766-69 for the method
ideas.where_published: Euler's canonical equation appears in his earlier papers on the addition of elliptic integrals and in Institutiones calculi integralis, vol. 1

ideas.what: Degenerate quartic with a double root at 0, A=B=0: integral of dx/(x sqrt(C+Dx+Ex^2)) in Lagrange form, with the observation that the y=0 normalization fails
ideas.modern_name: Degenerate (rational) case of the elliptic addition theorem
ideas.where_published: Likely only here and in related Euler papers on the Lagrange method

ideas.what: The substitution x -> 1/x maps the Lagrange integral for the coefficient-reversed polynomial onto itself
ideas.modern_name: Projective (Möbius) covariance of the Euler-Lagrange invariant of a binary quartic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Euler/Lagrange; made systematic in 19th-century invariant theory (Cayley, Hermite) and the theory of the Euler-Chasles correspondence
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Nova Acta Petrop. / Opuscula analytica)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine corollaries and consistency checks of the Lagrange integral for special cases (quadratic, double root, inversion). All of this is standard material in the history of the elliptic addition theorem; nothing appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Previous page, Theorem IV: the first integral's denominator should be (x-y)^2, not (x+y)^2.
Previous page: the constant in the '+' case should be 2√(AK), not 2√(Ak).
This page: the print does read 'BK' on the right-hand side, but this is a printer's error for 'Bk'.
Next page: 'dx/√(A+By+Cyy)' should read 'dy/√(A+By+Cyy)', and the '= 0' is missing.
